name: Execution from temporary directory
description: A process is running an executable from a world-writable temp location, a common malware staging and defense-evasion pattern.

name: Fileless or deleted-binary execution
description: The process executable was deleted after launch (memfd/self-deleting dropper), indicating in-memory payload execution.

name: Obfuscated or encoded command line
description: Command line contains encoded-content flags or base64 decode pipelines typical of obfuscated payloads.

name: Credential store access attempt
description: Command line references OS credential stores, consistent with credential dumping.

name: Suspicious download cradle
description: A download-and-execute pattern (curl/wget piped to an interpreter) is present in the command line.

name: Connection to known-malicious IP
description: An established connection to an IP on the IOC feed was observed.

name: Connection on classic C2 port
description: Outbound connection to a port frequently associated with commodity C2 frameworks and backdoors.

name: Possible reverse shell
description: A shell or scripting interpreter holds an established outbound connection to a non-standard port.

name: Shell listening on network port
description: A shell-like process is listening for inbound connections, consistent with a bind shell backdoor.

name: Sensitive account or auth file changed
description: An account, authentication, or privilege file was created or modified — potential persistence or account manipulation.

name: New content in startup or persistence location
description: A file was created in an autostart or persistence directory.

name: Executable written to temp directory
description: A new file appeared under a temp directory — common staging behavior.
